details: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) maintained the federal funds rate target at 3.50%-3.75% in June 2026. However, FOMC participants significantly increased their inflation forecasts compared to March, with the Core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation forecast rising to 3.3% for 2026. The median expectation for the federal funds rate path now indicates 12.5 basis points of hikes in 2026, projecting the rate to end 2026 at 3.75%. This signals a more hawkish outlook from the Fed as it aims for price stability, despite solid economic expansion and job gains.
title: US Federal Reserve's Hawkish Stance on Inflation May Lead to Rate Hikes

details: As of June 24, 2026, major digital assets saw widespread declines, reflecting a weakened market sentiment and reduced investor confidence. Bitcoin (BTC) fell by 1.53% to approximately $62,890.25, while Ethereum (ETH) dropped 2.75% to around $1,674.32. Other significant cryptocurrencies like XRP and Solana also experienced modest declines, indicating a general lack of upward momentum and prompting caution among investors.
title: Cryptocurrency Market Experiences Broad Losses Amid Weakened Sentiment

details: On June 23, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced further actions to dismantle overseas scam operations specifically targeting Americans. These transnational criminal organizations employ various cyber-enabled fraud schemes, with digital asset investment fraud being one of the most common and lucrative. A U.S. government estimate reported that Americans lost at least $10 billion in 2024 to Southeast Asia-based scam operations, a 66% increase over the previous year. The Treasury's ongoing efforts aim to combat these sophisticated scams and enhance financial security.
title: US Treasury Cracks Down on Digital Asset Scam Operations
